content.user_title: Diagnose Bugs with a Structured Loop
content.value_statement: Hard bugs waste time when teams guess before reproducing failures. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a disciplined debugging loop.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of a tight pass or fail feedback loop before diagnosis.
Prompts agents to reproduce and minimize the reported bug.
Structures ranked, falsifiable hypotheses before code changes.
Recommends targeted instrumentation tied to each hypothesis.
Directs agents to add regression coverage where a valid test seam exists.
Includes a human-in-the-loop shell template for manual UI reproduction.
limitations: Requires access to a codebase or artifact that can reproduce the issue.
Does not provide a debugger, profiler, or test runner by itself.
May need user input when a bug only appears in a protected environment.
Does not replace domain knowledge for ranking business-specific hypotheses.

use_cases.title: Fix a Reproducible Product Bug
use_cases.description: Use a tight failing loop to confirm the symptom, isolate the cause, and verify the fix.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Performance Regression
use_cases.description: Build a baseline, measure the slow path, and compare behavior across versions or configurations.

use_cases.title: Create a Clean Bug Handoff
use_cases.description: Capture the reproduction steps, minimized scenario, hypotheses, and test coverage for another maintainer.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Bug Diagnosis
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for a clear bug report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs skill. Build a tight reproduction loop for this bug before proposing a fix: [describe the symptom].

prompt_templates.title: Minimize a Reproduction
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow after a failing loop exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs skill to reduce this failing reproduction to the smallest scenario that still shows the reported symptom.

prompt_templates.title: Rank Debugging Hypotheses
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow when the failure is reproducible.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs skill. Generate 3 to 5 ranked hypotheses with falsifiable predictions before adding instrumentation.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Performance Regression
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for slow or unstable behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the diagnosing-bugs skill to establish a baseline, compare the regression path, test hypotheses, and add regression coverage where valid.

output_examples.input: A user reports that exporting a report fails only after filtering by date.
output_examples.output: The agent first creates a repeatable export loop, confirms the exact failure, minimizes the filter case, then ranks likely causes.

output_examples.input: A page became slower after a release, but no error appears.
output_examples.output: The agent measures a baseline, compares the old and new paths, avoids broad logging, and tests one performance hypothesis at a time.

output_examples.input: A flaky integration test fails in continuous integration but not locally.
output_examples.output: The agent raises the reproduction rate, records the observed failure mode, and only proceeds once the loop is useful.

best_practices: Create a command or script that catches the exact user symptom before changing code.
Change one variable at a time when testing hypotheses.
Remove temporary debug instrumentation before declaring the fix complete.
anti_patterns: Guessing at a fix before the bug is reproducible.
Adding broad logs that are not tied to a falsifiable prediction.
Writing a regression test at a seam that cannot exercise the real failure.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a bug, failing test, exception, flaky behavior, or performance regression needs structured diagnosis.

faq.question: Does the skill automatically fix bugs?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent through reproduction, hypothesis testing, instrumentation, fixing, and verification.

faq.question: Can it help with performance issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends baseline measurement, comparison, bisection, and profiler-friendly investigation before changing performance code.

faq.question: Does it require a test suite?
faq.answer: No. It can use tests, scripts, browser automation, CLI runs, traces, or human-in-the-loop prompts.

faq.question: How does it handle flaky bugs?
faq.answer: It focuses on raising the reproduction rate until the failure is frequent enough to guide diagnosis.

faq.question: What should I provide before using it?
faq.answer: Provide the symptom, affected environment, recent changes, logs, screenshots, or any artifact that helps reproduce the issue.
